# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only act on a wire, and currently have no tactile information beyond the three possible positions. Mute is the only teammate who can give me the manual in words, so I need that first. Deaf can see the bomb but cannot hear this request; Mute can coordinate the visual information with Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me the manual's complete instructions, including how to identify the correct wire and any needed communication code. I can cut wires 1, 2, or 3 once instructed.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is yellow. Three wires, ordered 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Deaf has supplied the visible configuration: display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still need Mute’s manual rule that maps these observations to the safe wire; I must not cut based on an assumption.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's configuration: display 0; yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please give the manual rule and the resulting wire number to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display still 0; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light has changed from yellow to orange. I received your single-finger gesture but do not know its meaning. Please indicate the required action clearly for Blind.

The light is now orange, while the display remains 0 and the wire order remains green, yellow, blue. Deaf needs a gesture code before any visual instruction will be meaningful, and I still require Mute’s manual instruction before touching a wire. I will relay the changed state to Mute and ask Mute to coordinate a clear agreed gesture with Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Updated visible state from Deaf: display 0; light ORANGE; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Deaf says a prior single-finger gesture had no established meaning. Please provide the manual's safe-cut rule/result and, if needed, establish an explicit gesture code with Deaf.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0; light green; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute has sent gestures, but their meaning is not established, so do not act on them yet.

The configuration has changed again: the light is now green, with display 0 and the same wire order. No manual instruction has reached me, and neither Mute’s nor any prior gesture has an agreed meaning for Deaf. I will relay the current state to Mute and continue to wait for the manual’s explicit safe action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Newest state from Deaf: display 0; GREEN light; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I will not cut until you give the manual's explicit rule/result. Please send it in words to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No verified instruction yet; do not act.

Mute cannot speak to me, so the only workable route is for Mute to encode the manual’s currently required wire as a conventional finger-number gesture, which Deaf can see and then report aloud. I will establish that convention with Mute: one raised finger means wire 1, two fingers means wire 2, and three fingers means wire 3. The current visible state is display 0, yellow light, wires green/yellow/blue.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Establish code now: after applying the manual to the CURRENT state (display 0, yellow light, wires green/yellow/blue), gesture ☝ for CUT WIRE 1, ✌ for CUT WIRE 2, or 🤟 for CUT WIRE 3. Send exactly one of those. Deaf can report which symbol you make.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; orange light; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled an upright index finger followed by thumbs-up, plausibly approving/selecting wire 1. This is not fully verified; use your manual-derived confirmation if available before acting.

Mute’s index-finger signal follows the wire-number convention I proposed, so it likely selected wire 1, but Mute could only have based that on the earlier yellow-light report. The light is currently orange, so I should not apply a recommendation for yellow to the changed state. I will ask Mute to make a fresh coded selection after hearing Deaf’s current orange-state report, and ask Deaf to relay the exact symbol.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your ☝ is understood as wire 1, but it appears based on the prior YELLOW-light report. Do not repeat an old answer. After hearing Deaf's current ORANGE state, apply the manual and send exactly ☝=wire1, ✌=wire2, or 🤟=wire3 for that state.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: display 0; light green; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's latest gesture is an open hand/palm, i.e. five. I do not know what action that code denotes.

The open-palm gesture is outside the three-symbol wire-selection code, so it cannot safely authorize a cut. The light is now green; since Mute acts before receiving this newest report, any selection for green can only arrive next round. I will require Mute to use only the established code and treat every other gesture as “do not cut.”

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely interpret 🖐. From now on, use ONLY one symbol after applying the manual to the latest state you know: ☝ means cut 1; ✌ means cut 2; 🤟 means cut 3. Any other gesture means DO NOT CUT. Deaf's newest state is display 0, GREEN light, wires green/yellow/blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: display 0; yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Full Mute-gesture timeline by light: yellow: two thumbs-up; orange: raised index; green: open palm, raised index, thumbs-up; yellow: none; orange: raised index, thumbs-up; green: open palm; yellow now: open palm. I cannot safely decode the gesture code.

The light has followed a stable cycle: yellow, orange, green, then yellow again. Because Mute receives my report one turn before I receive Mute’s answer, Mute must apply the manual to the *next* light in that cycle, not the reported one. The current report is yellow, so the next state should be orange. I will ask Mute for the manual’s orange-state wire using only the established three-wire code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Timing correction: light cycle is YELLOW→ORANGE→GREEN→YELLOW. Your answer arrives when the NEXT color is showing. Latest report is YELLOW, so send the manual's answer for ORANGE: ONLY ☝=cut wire 1, ✌=cut wire 2, or 🤟=cut wire 3. No extra gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Now: orange light, display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signals raised index finger again: likely select wire 1 (green).

The state is now orange exactly as anticipated, and Mute answered the orange-state request with the established `☝` code for wire 1. I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
